newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-INDIA STICK WITH ONE SPINNER FOR FIRST TEST.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-INDIA STICK WITH ONE SPINNER FOR FIRST TEST.

text.p: India resisted the temptation to play two spinners in their side for the opening test against South Africa when they announced a 12-man squad at Kingsmead on Wednesday.
Leg-spinner Anil Kumble, recently recovered from split webbing in his right hand, was an automatic selection as India's premier strike bowler along with paceman Javagal Srinath.

But left-arm spinner Venkatapathy Raju, tipped by some as a likely inclusion for the Durban test because of South Africa's occasional struggles against the turning ball in India, has been omitted from the 12.
Instead, India's attack will be led by seamers Srinath, Venkatesh Prasad and David Johnson, with the world-class threat of wrist-spinner Kumble their probable trump card.
Captain Sachin Tendulkar and Saurav Ganguly provide the back-up seam while opening batsman Woorkeri Raman can be employed with his occasional slow left-arm.
Batsman V.V.S.Laxman is expected to be named as 12th man at Kingsmead on Thursday.
India finished their preparation for the first test in a three-match series against South Africa with a three-hour work-out at Kingsmead on Christmas Day.
Captain Tendulkar, in confident mood after his side's recent 2-1 series victory at home, said his team were looking to keep the momentum going.
"We want to maintain the positive outlook which we had in India - where all three tests finished with results," Tendulkar said.
"It will also be imperative here in South Africa that our batsmen hit the loose ball whenever possible - and a positive outlook will help with this."
While India's test record has been disappointing away from home over the past decade, Tendulkar feels his side can now turn the corner.
"We haven't performed as well abroad as at home over the past 10 years, but I believe that India now has the batting and the bowling to do well abroad."
South Africa, who also completed their last-minute preparation with three hours of nets and fielding practice on Christmas Day, will only name their test side from a 13-man squad on Thursday morning.
Pacemen Allan Donald and Shaun Pollock are both available again after recovering from ankle injuries.

South Africa (from): Gary Kirsten, Andrew Hudson, Adam Bacher, Herschelle Gibbs, Daryll Cullinan, Hansie Cronje (captain), Jacques Kallis, Brian McMillan, Shaun Pollock, Lance Klusener, Dave Richardson, Allan Donald, Paul Adams.

India: Vikram Rathore, Woorkeri Raman, Saurav Ganguly, Sachin Tendulkar (captain), Rahul Dravid, Mohammad Azharuddin, Nayan Mongia, Anil Kumble, Javagal Srinath, David Johnson, Venkatesh Prasad, V.V.S.Laxman.
